growth_signal.value: Says it has served 2 million happy customers

entry.idea: People want to cut sugar and additives but still enjoy energy drinks, iced tea, and shakes, so HOLY sells powders and syrups you mix with water to make them yourself.
entry.lesson: Take a crowded, unhealthy consumer category and re-format the product itself (powder instead of a can) to be healthier, lighter to ship, and easier to sell directly online.
entry.name: HOLY

growth.basis: substitute: funding round bigger than the last (€10.5M Series A on top of a smaller earlier raise, for €12.3M total)
growth.reason: Its Series A was much bigger than its earlier funding, a sign investors believe it is growing fast, though no revenue or customer growth numbers are public.

market.reason: Soft drinks and energy drinks are bought by huge numbers of people worldwide.

tech.reason: It is a drink recipe and direct-to-consumer brand, which another company could copy without much difficulty.

sources.title: Germany-based HOLY raises €10.5M, aims to become Europe's leading healthy soft drink brand - Silicon Canals
Holy Company Information - Funding, Investors, and More

entry.twist: Selling concentrated powder and syrup instead of ready-made cans makes the drinks cheaper to ship and store, and lets HOLY sell variety packs straight to consumers online.
entry.who_pays: Everyday consumers who buy starter sets, refill packs, and subscriptions directly from HOLY's online store.
entry.why_now: More shoppers are avoiding sugary drinks, and direct-to-consumer brands can now reach them straight through their own website and social media instead of needing shelf space.
